target_customer: Retailers and shoppers in small physical stores; the company ran its own pop up store as a showcase
problem: Checkout lines and cashier labor slow physical retail, and Amazon Go showed a camera based alternative that small retailers could not build.
business_model: Autonomous store technology, initially operating its own store with plans to sell the system to retailers
product_category: Cashierless checkout and retail computer vision

founders.name: Tony Francis
education: Carnegie Mellon (met co-founder in machine learning classes)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2018-08-16) says the two founders met at Carnegie Mellon and later worked at Instagram and Uber without saying who worked where. The YC page says he later led the ML platform at Clubhouse and founded Dream3D (W23), and calls him a second time YC founder.

founders.name: Rameez Remsudeen
education: Carnegie Mellon (met co-founder in machine learning classes)
founders.background_notes: Named a founder in the TechCrunch article. A Village profile lists him as Inokyo co-founder from 2018-06 to 2019-12. Employer split between the two founders is not stated.

competitors.name: Amazon Go
competitors.what: Camera and weight sensor cashierless convenience stores

competitors.name: Standard Cognition
competitors.what: Camera based autonomous checkout sold to existing stores

competitors.name: AiFi
competitors.what: Camera based checkout that also flags suspicious behavior

competitors.name: BingoBox
competitors.what: Chinese unmanned stores using RFID tags

technical_complexity.rationale: Tracking shoppers and items with overhead and shelf cameras without facial recognition is a hard computer vision problem, and Amazon had years of head start.

defensibility.rationale: Little proprietary data or lock-in for a ten person team facing far better funded rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Amazon kept expanding Go, and rivals such as Zippin and AiFi raised larger rounds. Industry coverage reports the later closure of Grabango in 2024.

market_need_then: Amazon Go launched publicly in early 2018 and rivals sprang up in the US and China, showing retailer interest, though demand from small retailers was unproven.

branding.domain_note: inokyo.com; in this session the domain served an unrelated listing page, so the original site is not readable now.
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch described the Mountain View store as feeling like stealing, giving the brand early press.

brand_strength.rationale: One notable press piece and a pop up store, but no brand assets or community found and the name origin is unknown.

outcome_analysis: Inokyo opened a beta pop up store in Mountain View in August 2018 with press coverage but only about 120K in recorded funding. It faced Amazon, Standard Cognition and AiFi with far more capital. The YC directory lists it as inactive and the CEO later founded Dream3D, but no shutdown notice states the cause, so the failure factors are inferences from the competitive record and the lack of any later round.
notes: The 120K round dated 2018-05 rests on CB Insights (Soma Capital named only on a comparison page); TechCrunch only says YC provided seed funding. No later round found. The shutdown cause is not public; failure factors are inferred, not sourced. TechCrunch dated 2018-08 is a few months after the S18 batch start, used for competitors.
